# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Keep the records to a minimum (one or two lines)
3.  For more formal investigations, 

## Additional notes for accurately documenting fire-safety checks	

Be sure that you keep track of the inspection records as you go. Always list the critical parameters (see next section).  Once you have collected the data from your inspection, immediately write them down.  You can use any of the formats such as: building plan, drawings, maps, etc.  This will provide you with evidence of your inspection.  Start with the inspection records first, and then move on to the more formal documents.  Once you have completed the inspection record, you may want to upload it and archive it.  If you don't have a computer or an internet connection at the inspection site, you can use a blank sheet of paper.  You don't need a computer as every cell phone has a camera.

- **Inspections
